# CSU Channel Islands

- **Introduction to Data Science** (DATA 200)\
  Spring 2026: [Syllabus](https://docs.google.com/document/d/148lpz-vpAX8LIx_GxwIQjmcQJIawsVZOSq8nEV0YZPY/edit?usp=sharing), [Lectures {{< fa brands github >}}](https://github.com/csuci-data200-spring2026/lectures)\
  Fall 2025: [Syllabus](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iqrVrfYycfpV3MnY97QQmcw7qq57TDBKslZnU6VvFKU/edit?usp=sharing), [Lectures {{< fa brands github >}}](https://github.com/csuci-data200/lectures)\
  Foundations of the practice of data science. Exploration and implementation of the data science life cycle in locally relevant contexts. Emphasis on statistical thinking and computer programming required to collect, prepare and analyze data numerically, visually and algorithmically, and to ethically communicate findings. Introduction to machine learning. 
  
- **Elementary Statistics** (MATH 201)\
  Spring 2026 [Syllabus](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1R5frq-VUGpNhoZQorHk-rTARcs5qt4Gy3181Oz51_Vw/edit?usp=sharing)\
  Critical reasoning using a quantitative and statistical, problem-solving approach to solving real-world problems. Topics include: probability and statistics, sample data, probability and empirical data distributions, sampling techniques, estimation and hypothesis testing, ANOVA, and correlation and regression analysis. Students will use standard statistical software to analyze real-world and simulated data.
  
- **Probability and Statistics** (MATH 352)\
  Spring 2026: [Syllabus](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aSCkyVWfp9vKyGs5BbnEG26AG2fV8UUW14saw36VyWk/edit?usp=sharing)\
  Critical reasoning using a quantitative and statistical, problem-solving approach to solving real-world problems. Topics include: probability and statistics, sample data, probability and empirical data distributions, sampling techniques, estimation and hypothesis testing, ANOVA, and correlation and regression analysis. Students will use standard statistical software to analyze real-world and simulated data.
  
- **Statistical Models** (MATH 430)\
  Fall 2025: [Syllabus](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mgDjIgYG-hoV6fMIc6Yw9dvmGBToZOA-V5c0U1OUJx8/edit?usp=sharing), [Lectures {{< fa brands github >}}](https://github.com/csuci-math430/lectures)\
  Discussion of experimental design, sampling methods, data collection, and methods of data analysis related to scientific fields.

# Past Teaching Experience

## Guest Lecturer

### CSU Long Beach

- **Regression Analysis** (STAT 510) - *graduate* \
  Fall 2024:\
  Introduced logistic regression across two class sessions, and held a corresponding office hour. Observed by Dr. Seungjoon (Joon) Lee as part of the [CSU Pre-Professor Program](https://grad.uci.edu/professional-development/graduate-and-postdoctoral-scholar-resource-center/csu-long-beach-pre-professor-program/).
  
- **Community Health Statistics** (H SC 403) - *undergraduate*\
  Fall 2024:\
  Introduced Chi-Square test for Goodness of Fit and the Chi-Square Test for Independence in one class session. Observed by Dr. Selena Nguyen-Rodriguez as part of the [CSU Pre-Professor Program](https://grad.uci.edu/professional-development/graduate-and-postdoctoral-scholar-resource-center/csu-long-beach-pre-professor-program/).

## Instructor of Record

### UC Irvine

-   **Basic Statistics** (Stats 7) \
    2022 Summer Session:\
    Introduces basic inferential statistics including confidence intervals and hypothesis testing on means and proportions, t-distribution, Chi Square, regression and correlation. F-distribution and nonparametric statistics included if time permits.

### University of Nevada, Reno

-   **Intermediate Algebra** (Math 96)\
    2019 Summer:\
    Basic properties of the real numbers; standard algebraic techniques, including exponents, factoring, fractions, radicals; problem solving; linear and quadratic equations; the concept of graphing.
-   **Elementary Algebra** (Math 95)\
    2019 Summer:\
    Preparation for Intermediate Algebra. Topics include the fundamental operations on real numbers, inequalities in one variable, polynomials, integer exponents, and solving quadratic equations by factoring.
